item.title: FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library
item.description:
FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library

FastMCP 3.2 extends Calibre e‑book library with AI‑assisted search, RAG, and agentic workflows.

🔍 Overview

  • AI‑assisted search, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG), and agentic workflows for Sandra’s 1000+ book library.
  • Exposes 33 portmanteau tools for natural‑language library management.
  • Built into Calibre’s core engine.

🧩 How it works

  • Bridges Calibre e‑book library and AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol.
  • Reads Calibre’s metadata.db directly and indexes metadata for semantic search using LanceDB.
  • Provides Incremental LanceDB RAG Sync and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) hybrid search.
  • Offers a 21‑tool registry and a portmanteau CRUD & Library Health Engine.

⚙️ Key details

  • FastMCP 3.2 Server (port :10720) and WebApp (Next.js 15 on :10721).
  • Calibre GUI + Plugin (Qt6 / PyQt5).
  • FastAPI REST layer with async background workers.
  • CALIBRE CONTENT SERVER (e.g., :8099, http://goliath:8099/ or http://localhost:8080/).
  • Async Python Engine (calibre.srv) and RapydScript SPA (index-generated.html).
  • HTML5 In‑Browser Reader (viewer.js / offline SW) and OPDS Mobile Catalog Feed.
  • Databases: metadata.db (Calibre SQLite catalog), full-text-search.db (FTS5 token index), calibre_mcp_data.db (sidecar extended metadata).
  • Semantic search powered by LanceDB, fastembed (BAAI/bge-small), and Ollama/OpenAI providers.

🚀 Availability

  • Download Calibre MCP_*_x64-setup.exe from Releases, double‑click to launch Calibre MCP.
  • Claude Desktop one‑liner: download calibre‑mcp.mcpb from Releases and install via Settings → MCP Servers → Install from file.
  • After installation, use prompts such as “Find unread sci‑fi books”, “Open a random Banks novel”, or “What’s my library health?”.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides AI‑powered semantic search and natural‑language library management directly within Calibre.
  • Enables RAG and agentic workflows to help users navigate large e‑book collections efficiently.

#Calibre #AI #LanceDB #SemanticSearch #Python

Source: sandraschi/calibremcp

item.title: Databricks Introduces Agentic Identity Resolution for Customer Data Platforms
item.description:
Databricks Introduces Agentic Identity Resolution for Customer Data Platforms

📚 Introduction

Databricks has launched Agentic Identity Resolution, an approach that combines deterministic, probabilistic, and LLM-based matching to connect fragmented customer records. This capability is part of CustomerLake, designed to help data teams build trusted datasets and enable marketers to activate audiences faster.

🧩 How It Works

The process involves several steps:

  • Run deterministic rules first (exact email, exact phone, a partner ID that maps to your customer ID), then score the gaps with probabilistic matching.
  • Cluster the matches and mint, or keep, a persistent ID.
  • Build layers using Spark Declarative Pipelines and run identity resolution after silver, with the canonical ID becoming the join key for gold.

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Agentic Identity Resolution Combines deterministic, probabilistic, and LLM-based matching to connect fragmented records
Profile Agents Handle heavy lifting of matching and golden-record survivorship
Manual data steward overrides Allow teams to apply human judgment where needed

Agentic CDP requires:

  • The right sources, clean data, one identity per customer, and golden profiles marketers trust.
  • Agents handle matching records and drafting audiences while people choose sources, review matches, and approve actions.
  • Identity resolution runs next to data, making ownership of the identity graph practical.

📏 Data Model Approach

  • Part 1 of a two-part series focusing on modeling from raw data to omnichannel activation.
  • Part 2 covers mapping B2C and B2B datasets, attributes, and use cases onto the model.
  • Identity is matched nightly inside a tool, owned, explainable and reversible, with an audit-able identity graph using a persistent ID.

🚀 Availability

  • Can be built with SQL rules plus open-source matchers like Splink or Zingg.
  • Or use CustomerLake, where Profile Agents handle the heavy lifting.
  • Data teams can define trusted datasets once through Databricks and Unity Catalog.

💡 Why It Matters

Brands long asked why they couldn’t own their identity graph and run deterministic matching on their own data. With identity resolution running next to the data, owning the graph becomes practical, and in our experience it’s the most important table you’ll build.

#AIagents #CDP #CustomerData #IdentityResolution #Databricks

Source: Data Modeling Best Practices for an Agentic CDP, Part 1: The Data Foundation

item.title: Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg
item.description:
Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg

Databricks announced support for catalog labels, a new capability in the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API that enables platforms, engines, and agents to access context such as business purpose, ownership, and data classifications maintained in Iceberg REST-compatible catalogs. This development addresses the issue of metadata context remaining siloed in source catalogs, which previously forced teams to recreate classifications across platforms or maintain custom metadata synchronization pipelines.

🧩 How it works

Databricks worked with the Apache Iceberg community to add an optional labels field to the Iceberg REST LoadTable response. This provides a standard way for catalogs to expose table- and column-level context to other platforms, tools, and agents.

  • Labels format: String key-value pairs that describe business ownership, intended use, sensitivity, or other catalog-maintained context.
  • Flexibility: The standard defines a common format for sharing metadata without prescribing vocabulary or interpretation, allowing each platform to build on it in its own way.
  • Example: A table named support_cases can carry labels like domain=customer_support or system.certification_status=certified. An authorized data steward can also assign column-level labels, such as content_type=support_case_summary for an issue_summary column.

⚙️ Key details

Tag Exchange is Databricks’ implementation of this standard, exposing Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. This makes catalog metadata available directly to Python applications, including data-discovery tools and agents.

  • Open Governance: Context maintained in one system becomes usable across every platform, engine, and AI agent working with the data.
  • Reusability: Enterprises can reuse classifications and business context for discovery, agent workflows, and access policies.
  • Interoperability: Each tool retains the freedom to decide how to interpret and use that context, while the catalog’s metadata remains intact across platforms.

Databricks is joined by Google Cloud, Salesforce, ClickHouse, Atlan, Collibra, DataHub, Immuta, Trust3 AI, PhoenixAI, and Datastrato in advancing this shared vision of metadata interoperability.

🚀 Availability

Tag Exchange is available in Beta today. To get started, users can enable “Tag Exchange via Iceberg REST Catalog” in the Databricks Previews portal.

💡 Why it matters

This capability allows sensitivity labels set once in Unity Catalog to drive policy in external platforms without separate metadata projects. As noted by Don Bosco Durai, CTO of Trust3 AI, a sensitivity label set once in Unity Catalog can now drive policy in platforms like Trust3 AI without a separate metadata project. Similarly, Chandru Sugunan, Director of Product at Atlan, noted that open metadata exchange through the Iceberg REST Catalog lets enterprises keep context intact across every platform they choose to run.

#Databricks #ApacheIceberg #Metadata #TagExchange #DataGovernance #Interoperability

Source: Sharing catalog metadata across data platforms, engines, and agents

item.title: New Standards and Tools Emerge to Manage Enterprise AI Token Costs
item.description:
New Standards and Tools Emerge to Manage Enterprise AI Token Costs

The Linux Foundation has launched the Tokenomics Foundation to develop open standards for AI cost economics, signaling that managing the economics of AI is now an industry discipline. As enterprises scale AI on platforms like Amazon Bedrock, token spend often grows even as per-token prices fall, creating a need for better cost allocation and management tools.

🔍 The Problem with AI Cost Visibility

Without cost allocation tags, cloud invoices show AI spend as a single line item rather than broken down by team, workload, agent, or model. This lack of visibility makes it difficult to connect consumption to accountable owners or business outcomes. The Linux Foundation’s new initiative aims to address this by establishing standards for what is now considered an industry discipline in AI cost economics.

⚙️ Managing Amazon Bedrock Costs

AWS and Accenture recommend a phased approach to managing AI costs, applying each phase independently to workloads where it will have the most impact. Key mechanisms include:

  • Cost Allocation Tags: Applied through Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles, these tags (by team, cost center, and environment) allow tracking of which teams, applications, and agents drive spend once activated in the AWS Billing console.
  • Reporting and Logging: AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR 2.0) handle financial attribution, breaking down billed inference costs by workload and team. Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging records request-level details, including model used and token counts, while Amazon CloudWatch captures operational signals like invocation counts and latency.
  • Cost per Business Transaction (CpBT): This metric aggregates all model invocations, retries, tool calls, and agent handoffs contributing to one successful business output into a single fully loaded cost figure. It surfaces the true cost of producing a result, including failed attempts, and helps distinguish between spend driven by scaling success versus waste.

🧩 Optimization Levers

Specific technical levers can significantly reduce token spend. In four client engagements across telecom, insurance, mining, and a large enterprise deployment, Accenture applied these levers, measuring token spend reductions of about 40–85 percent.

  • Prompt Caching: Amazon Bedrock reuses parts of prompts that repeat across requests (e.g., system instructions, tool definitions), storing key-value state to skip recomputation. This is designed to reduce cached input token costs by up to 90 percent for supported models.
  • Batch Inference: For non-urgent workloads, Amazon Bedrock batch inference processes requests asynchronously as a group at 50 percent lower cost than on-demand pricing for select models. Results are written to Amazon S3, making it suitable for nightly reports and document processing pipelines.
  • Intelligent Prompt Routing: This feature directs requests across models within the same family, matching tasks to the level of intelligence required by business value, complexity, and risk. It can reduce costs by up to 30 percent without compromising accuracy.

💡 Azure Databricks Genie Integration

Azure Databricks offers a complementary approach through Genie, which brings governed data into Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Excel, and Copilot Studio.

  • Free Allowance: Every identified user gets $10 of free Genie usage each month, which resets on the first of every month. Through January 31, 2027, Genie One and Genie Agents are free for users, directing the full allowance to Genie Code. After that, the allowance is shared across all Genie products.
  • Budgets: Admins can set budgets to control pay-as-you-go spend above the free allowance. These budgets track spend in near real-time and block new requests once a threshold is reached, though they are designed for control rather than as absolute caps, and warehouse compute is billed separately.
  • Integration: The Genie Plugin, now generally available, allows partners to integrate Genie into customer environments quickly. When plugged into Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot routes questions Genie can answer to Genie, preventing duplicate costs on the Copilot side.

#AIGovernance #CostOptimization #AmazonBedrock #AzureDatabricks #Tokenomics

Source: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach | Amazon Web Services Source: How partners use Genie’s free tier on Azure Databricks

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with New Read-Your-Writes Consistency Feature
item.description:
PostgreSQL 19 Released with New Read-Your-Writes Consistency Feature

PostgreSQL 19 has been released, arriving two months later than the typical September schedule due to a flurry of issues related to AI-reported vulnerabilities.

🔍 Overview

  • The release was delayed from September by two months.
  • The delay was attributed to addressing ongoing AI-reported vulnerability issues.
  • The author considers the release “definitely worth the wait.”

🧩 How it works

The release introduces a “read-your-writes” consistency feature for applications sending reads to standbys using the new WAIT FOR LSN command. This allows a session on a standby to wait until it has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query. This ensures the application can read data it just wrote on the primary.

Example Workflow

  1. Update a record on the primary: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama';
  2. Get the current LSN: SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); (returns a value like 0/0306EE20).
  3. Store the LSN value (e.g., in a signed cookie).
  4. On a subsequent request, use the stored LSN on a standby: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s');
  5. Run the query: SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama';

The timeout parameter is optional. If provided, the system returns an error if the replica does not catch up within the specified time.

💡 Why it matters

This pattern ensures users see events in chronological order and maintain a consistent view across subsequent requests. Similar patterns have previously been implemented in hand-rolled solutions:

  • Wikipedia/MediaWiki: Uses a hand-rolled version against MySQL replication, saving the primary binlog position in the session and waiting for replicas to catch up before reads. MediaWiki now uses MySQL’s WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET() function and falls back to SOURCE_POS_WAIT().

#PostgreSQL #Database #SQL #DataConsistency #WaitForLSN

Source: PostgreSQL 19 Released

item.title: JamAI Base: Open-source RAG platform with built-in LLM capabilities
item.description:
JamAI Base: Open-source RAG platform with built-in LLM capabilities

JamAI Base is an open-source RAG backend platform that integrates an embedded database and vector database with managed memory and RAG capabilities.

🔍 Overview

  • Open-source RAG backend platform
  • Integrates embedded database (SQLite) and vector database (LanceDB)
  • Features built-in LLM, vector embeddings, and reranker orchestration
  • Accessible through a spreadsheet-like UI and REST API

🧩 How it works

  • Transform static database tables into dynamic, AI-enhanced entities
  • Automatically populate columns with relevant data generated by LLMs
  • Built-in REST API endpoint for streamlining AI integration
  • Facilitate real-time interactions between frontend and LLM backend
  • Eliminate manual backend management of user inputs and outputs
  • Enable sophisticated LLM workflows
  • Act as repositories for structured data and documents
  • Enhance LLM’s contextual understanding
  • Upload and synchronize documents and data
  • Simplify creation and management of intelligent chatbot applications
  • Integrate with RAG to utilize content from any Knowledge Table
  • Store, manage, query, and retrieve embeddings on large-scale multi-modal data
  • Ensure optimal performance and seamless scalability

⚙️ Key details

  • Focus on defining ‘what’ you want to achieve rather than ‘how’
  • Allow users to define relationships and desired outcomes
  • Eliminate the need to write procedures
  • Built on LanceDB, an open-source vector database for AI workloads
  • Serverless design for optimal performance and scalability
  • Supports any LLMs, including OpenAI GPT-4, Anthropic Claude 3, and Meta Llama3
  • Built-in RAG features, no need to build the RAG pipeline yourself
  • Combines keyword-based search, structured search, and vector search
  • Automatically determines the best way to chunk your data
  • Leverages multi-lingual, multi-functional, and multi-granular text embeddings for free

🚀 Availability

  • Sign up for a free account
  • Get free LLM tokens
  • Build a basic chatbot without any backend setup

#RAG #LLM #AI #OpenSource #Chatbot

Source: EmbeddedLLM/JamAIBase

item.title: New Reversibility Classes Framework for Tool-Using AI Agents
item.description:
New Reversibility Classes Framework for Tool-Using AI Agents

Tool-using AI agents can change files, databases, access rights, and public information, yet current permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone.

🔍 Overview

Researchers present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary designed to address the gap between tool permissions and undo capabilities. This framework introduces argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults, and an explicit prior-state capture contract.

🧩 How it works

The implementation includes a pinned repository and an evidence-linked registry covering 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. The system validates rules through specific checks:

  • All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations.
  • Native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools.
  • One AI-assisted reviewer approved 148 ratings, with 75 matching the registry; however, this is noted as not independent agreement.

⚙️ Key details

Testing on 2,158 recorded runs demonstrated the effectiveness of the implemented session guard:

  • The guard gated the associated action in all 29 attributable attack-positive runs.
  • In comparison, a read/write proxy handled only 18 of those runs.
  • The system added nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs.

Experiments involving controlled file operations, Git, SQLite, and three browsers revealed that recovery depends on captured state, later changes, editor storage, and recovery route. These experiments also exposed a Git merge-state exception.

💡 Why it matters

The evidence supports making recovery assumptions explicit and testable. However, the study does not establish registry-wide accuracy, reduced production harm, or general recovery reliability.

#AIAgents #ReversibilityClasses #MCPServers #AISafety

Source: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions

item.title: Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases
item.description:
Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases

Attu 3.0, an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases, has been released, expanding the visual experience for Milvus 3.0 while retaining compatibility with Milvus 2.6.0+ and Zilliz Cloud.

🔍 Overview

  • Attu is an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus clusters from a single instance, browse collections, run vector searches, manage backups, monitor health, and chat with an AI agent that understands your data.

🚀 Availability

  • Available as a web app (Docker, Kubernetes, or a standalone server package) or desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows).
  • Attu v3.0 supports Zilliz Cloud and open-source Milvus 2.6.0+ and 3.x.
  • Milvus 2.5.x and earlier are not supported.
  • The v3.0.0 release includes a non-Docker, non-Electron server package for Linux x64.

⚙️ Key details

  • Explore Parquet and Iceberg data without copying it into Milvus, refresh external schemas and data, and browse or restore Collection Snapshots.
  • Work with Milvus TEXT fields, add or remove supported fields, edit descriptions, and manage Function Fields from the Schema page.
  • Run Query and Search aggregations, group and order results, paginate large result sets, and apply Function Score reranking.
  • Configure MinHash Function Fields and MINHASH_LSH indexes to find near-duplicate documents from raw text.
  • Register reusable dictionaries, stop-word lists, synonym lists, and tokenizer resources.
  • Load or release individual partitions, configure entity-level TTL, export complete Collections, and import large files in chunks.
  • The Docker image stores its SQLite database at /data/attu.db by default.
  • The -v attu-data:/data volume persists your saved connections, agent conversations, and preferences across container restarts.
  • The image runs as the non-root node user (uid=1000, gid=1000), so named volumes are recommended.
  • On SELinux-enabled hosts, also add the :Z mount option: ./attu-data:/data:Z.
  • The non-Docker server package requires Node.js 24.x and includes the Attu server bundle and bin/milvus-backup.
  • The launcher defaults to 0.0.0.0:3080.
  • Set HOST, PORT, ATTU_DATA_DIR, or ATTU_DB_PATH to customize the runtime paths and listener.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus instances from a single Attu deployment.
  • Add, edit, and switch between connections in the sidebar.
  • Each cluster has its own dedicated workspace with independent monitoring, agent sessions, and preferences, ideal for managing dev, staging, and production environments side by side.
  • Browse databases and collections, view and edit data inline, import/export in CSV, JSON, and Parquet formats.
  • Interactive vector similarity search with configurable embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Jina, VoyageAI, and more).

#Milvus #VectorDatabases #AIManagement #Attu #DataScience

Source: zilliztech/attu

item.title: Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support
item.description:
Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support

On November 15, 2026, developers shared updates on the progress of the Datasette 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete. The latest release includes significant architectural changes, security patches, and user interface enhancements developed with assistance from Claude Fable 5.2.

⚙️ Key details

The release introduces several functional improvements to the platform’s core data handling and display capabilities:

  • Streaming Support: Output renderers, including built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms, now utilize streaming.
  • Plugin API: A new Response.stream() method allows plugins to register as capable of streaming every row in a table in a single operation.
  • JSON Redesign: The row page JSON representation has been redesigned for the 1.0 standard, and JSON data within columns can now be pretty-printed.
  • UI Components: A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component has been added to provide copy-schema functionality in various locations.

🧩 How it works

A major feature in this release is the implementation of CSS multi-page view transitions, which allow the multi-page application to behave more like a single-page application (SPA).

Component Mechanism
.facet-results Morphs from old position to new position during transition.
.table-wrapper Morphs position if it contains .rows-and-columns.
DatasetteModal.confirm() A new JavaScript utility method for handling confirmations.

These transitions are enabled for users who do not have “prefers-reduced-motion” active. This functionality currently works in Safari and Chrome.

🛡️ Security and Improvements

This update addresses dozens of bugs and includes a specific security fix regarding private stored queries. A GitHub advisory was issued because private stored queries could previously be exposed, revealing the title and SQL of the query, though they could not be executed by unauthorized parties.

General bug fixes were supported by several contributors, including:

  • Zihan Dai
  • Peter Olkhovets
  • Ilya Khalafi
  • Ankita Advitot

🚀 Availability

While currently available for Safari and Chrome users, Firefox support for the new CSS view transitions is expected to arrive on December 8th, 2026, with the release of Firefox 162. These features are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.

#Datasette #OpenSource #WebDevelopment

Source: Release: datasette 1.0a43

item.title: Security Update Resolves Unauthorized Access in Database Registration Routing
item.description:
Security Update Resolves Unauthorized Access in Database Registration Routing

A minor security fix has been backported from version 1.0a43 to address a vulnerability that allowed unauthorized database downloads. This update resolves a security issue occurring when database routes and names do not match.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Registration: The issue involves databases registered using add_database(db, name=..., route=...).
  • Vulnerability Condition: The security flaw occurred when a database was registered with a route that differed from its name.
  • Access Restriction Bypass: In these instances, actors who were denied access to the database could still download it from the /<route>.db endpoint.

🚀 Availability

  • The security fix was backported from version 1.0a43.

#Cybersecurity #Database #SoftwarePatch

Source: Release: datasette 0.65.6

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base adds fine-grained access control and migration tools
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base adds fine-grained access control and migration tools

Amazon Bedrock now provides a Managed Knowledge Base service that handles ingestion, storage, indexing, and retrieval. This service includes built-in features such as hybrid search, a managed reranker, and multimodal file parsing, with infrastructure that scales automatically based on content volume.

🧩 How it works

Managed Knowledge Base simplifies content management by handling technical infrastructure, while allowing teams to retain control over their content and applications. The service integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose knowledge bases as tools for agents.

Feature Function
ACL awareness Filters retrieval results based on user permissions
Agentic retrieval Handles multi-part questions and iterative searching
Deletion safeguard Protects against accidental bulk removal of indexed content
Native connectors Ingests from S3, SharePoint, and Confluence

⚙️ Key details

  • Migration Support: A new migration guide in the Agent Toolkit for AWS helps teams migrate from customer-managed knowledge bases to the managed service. The process includes read-only discovery, planning, and the generation of infrastructure-as-code templates.
  • Access Control: The system supports Access Control List (ACL) awareness, which ingests document permissions alongside content. When integrated with AgentCore Gateway, the system can inject verified user attributes into tool calls to ensure users only access authorized documents.
  • Security Layers: Security is maintained through a combination of request interceptors that define user context, Cedar policies within AgentCore, and resource-based policies that restrict access to the gateway execution role.
  • Pricing: The service uses usage-based pricing, with costs metered directly based on stored and retrieved content.

🚀 Availability

  • Supports up to 200 data sources per knowledge base.
  • Supports up to 10,000 knowledge bases per account, per Region.
  • Integration with AgentCore Gateway and resource-based policies are exclusive to Managed Knowledge Base.

#AmazonBedrock #GenerativeAI #CloudComputing #DataSecurity

Source: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent | Amazon Web Services Source: Fine-grained access control for Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base tools | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon Quick adds unified conversational AI over structured and unstructured data
item.description:
Amazon Quick adds unified conversational AI over structured and unstructured data

Amazon Quick addresses this with a unified experience.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Quick lets you connect structured data through enriched datasets and unstructured data through S3‑backed knowledge bases, then query both through a single conversational AI agent.

🧩 How it works

  • Unstructured content (documents, PDFs, reports) is stored in Amazon S3 and indexed through a knowledge base.
  • Structured data (metrics, sales figures, operational KPIs) is loaded as enriched datasets with semantic descriptions that the agent uses to translate questions into SQL.
  • A Space brings both data types together into a single workspace. The Space references your knowledge base for unstructured queries and your datasets for structured queries, and can also include dashboards, file uploads, and action connectors.
  • A custom chat agent links to the Space, uses it as its knowledge source, determines whether to query the knowledge base, the dataset, or both, and returns a combined response with citations.
  • AI guardrails such as content‑safety screening are applied to chat interactions.
  • Adding a new data source to the Space makes it instantly usable by the linked agent, while responses respect the permissions of the requesting user.

⚙️ Key Details

  • An Amazon Quick account with an Enterprise subscription is required to create datasets.
  • In the admin console, an administrator chooses Permissions → AWS resources → Amazon S3 → Select S3 buckets; selected buckets have read‑only permissions by default.
  • Permissions are needed to create integrations, knowledge bases, datasets, spaces, and chat agents.
  • Setup steps:
    1. Start by connecting Amazon Quick to your S3 bucket.
    2. In the Amazon Quick console, select Knowledge in the left navigation panel.
    3. Choose the Amazon S3 connector and click Add.
    4. Provide the S3 bucket URL (the bucket must be in the same Region as Amazon Quick).
    5. Decide whether to use ACLs before creating the knowledge base (cannot be changed later).
    6. A success banner confirms the integration and the knowledge base begins indexing in the background.
    7. Load a structured file (e.g., Product_Sales.csv) as a dataset.
    8. Enrich the dataset with semantic descriptions, custom instructions, and correct data types so the AI can translate natural‑language questions into SQL.
  • The layer where data from different sources converges into a unified context is the Space.

🗂 Component Summary

Component Purpose
Knowledge Base Indexes unstructured content stored in Amazon S3 for AI‑powered search
Enriched Dataset Holds structured data with semantic descriptions; enables SQL translation
Space Workspace that references both the knowledge base and datasets; may include dashboards, file uploads, action connectors
Custom Chat Agent Links to a Space, decides which source(s) to query, returns combined response with citations
Permissions Controls access to S3 buckets, datasets, and ensures responses respect user permissions

🚀 Availability

  • Requires an Enterprise subscription for dataset creation.
  • The S3 bucket must reside in the same AWS Region as Amazon Quick.
  • All components (knowledge bases, datasets, spaces, chat agents) are created through the Amazon Quick console.

#AmazonQuick #ConversationalAI #DataIntegration

Source: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services Source: How Gen Digital built Norton Revamp’s AI-curated News Engine with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search | Amazon Web Services Source: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI with EDB Postgres AI and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Data Lineage Becomes Core Security Perimeter for Agentic AI
item.description:
Data Lineage Becomes Core Security Perimeter for Agentic AI

A recent workflow failure showed that when an AI agent pulls data from multiple internal sources and hands it off to another agent without human oversight, sensitive and confidential information can leak undetected. The incident highlights why AI governance must evolve to focus on data visibility rather than just tools.

🔍 Overview

  • A sales representative asked an AI agent for customer pricing.
  • The agent aggregated data from restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes.
  • A second AI agent used that aggregated data to draft a proposal.
  • No human checks were applied at either handoff.
  • The final proposal contained unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, and the source of the problematic data could not be traced.
  • This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically.

🛡️ Data Lineage as the New Security Perimeter

  • “Data lineage is the new security perimeter, providing the visibility needed for governance, accountability, and trust, without impeding AI adoption at scale.”
  • It offers the ability to trace how data moves, is copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed.
  • Establishing data lineage enables teams to manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows.

⚙️ How Agentic AI Exposes Data Visibility Gaps

  • Enterprises using agentic AI are dealing with moving and fragmented data, not just static files.
  • Traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient.
  • Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves.

📈 Implications for Governance

  • AI security is fundamentally a data visibility problem, not a tool problem.
  • Without clear data lineage, organizations cannot trace where sensitive data entered a workflow or how it spread.
  • Rapid, dynamic governance mechanisms are needed to keep pace with continuous data transformation in AI‑driven processes.

🚀 Path Forward

  • Teams should prioritize establishing comprehensive data lineage.
  • Governance frameworks must account for the ingestion, copying, summarizing, transformation, reuse, and redistribution of data across agents.
  • By focusing on data visibility, organizations can maintain trust and accountability while scaling AI adoption.

#AIgovernance #DataLineage #AgenticAI #Security #EnterpriseAI

item.title: Indegene Deploys LLM‑Powered Data Quality Agent on AWS for Life Sciences
item.description:
Indegene Deploys LLM‑Powered Data Quality Agent on AWS for Life Sciences

Indegene has launched a production‑grade, large language model (LLM)‑powered Data Quality Agent inside its NEXT Unified Data Platform (NEXT UDP) on Amazon Web Services. The agent automatically creates context‑aware data‑quality rules, validates them, and generates ready‑to‑run SQL and Python code, all under a centralized, human‑in‑the‑loop governance model.

🔍 Overview

  • Indegene Limited (BSE: 544172, NSE: INDGN) is the strategic operating partner to the life‑sciences industry, serving the world’s top 20 biopharma companies.
  • NEXT UDP is an AI‑driven data platform that unifies commercial, medical, clinical, and enterprise data into a governed environment.
  • The platform includes a suite of standalone AI agents; the Data Quality agent is the focus of this update.

🧩 How it works

  1. Data profiling – The agent examines a new dataset to understand its structure and content.
  2. Rule generation – Using LLM reasoning, it produces context‑aware technical and business rules (e.g., HCP ID format, product market‑share totals).
  3. Validation – Generated rules are automatically validated against the data.
  4. Code output – The agent emits executable SQL and Python scripts that implement the validated rules.
  5. Governance – All outputs are subject to human‑in‑the‑loop review before deployment, satisfying strict life‑science compliance requirements.

⚙️ Key capabilities

  • Context‑aware rule creation – blends technical checks (null, format, uniqueness) with business logic (market‑share percentages, specialty‑aligned prescription activity).

item.title: Integrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Denodo for Federated Data Access
item.description:
Integrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Denodo for Federated Data Access

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Denodo Platform are being used to build and optimize AI agents capable of accessing distributed enterprise data through a semantic layer.

🧩 How it works

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosts the agent, manages inbound authentication, and handles the outbound credentials presented to Denodo. The system operates as follows:

  • Planning: A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock plans and writes queries.
  • Communication: The agent communicates with the semantic layer using VQL, which is Denodo’s SQL dialect.
  • Exposure: The Denodo MCP Server uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to expose governed views to the agent.
  • Reasoning: Joins, metric definitions, and row and column filters are maintained within the semantic layer rather than the prompt.

⚙️ Key details

Denodo implements the semantic layer as a data virtualization platform. This allows the agent to access a source mix that includes both cloud and on-premises data, meaning federation is not bounded by an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).

Component Function
Denodo Virtual DataPort (VDP) The core query engine where semantic-layer objects live, VQL executes, and access policies evaluate.
Design Studio The browser-based authoring surface for VDP.

Data Federation Example

In a scenario where data is distributed across different engines without foreign keys spanning them or ETL jobs to build them, Denodo plans the federated query at execution time to reconcile the shared identifier (cid):

  • Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible): Customer profile data.
  • Amazon Redshift: Order history.
  • On-premises PostgreSQL: Rewards program data (rewards_account).

Denodo decides what to push into Aurora and Amazon Redshift, what to fetch from the on-premises cluster, and how to combine results without moving data between sources.

🚀 Availability

Denodo on AWS offers two deployment options:

  • Agora: A fully managed cloud service.
  • Self-managed installation: Deployed on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS).

#AmazonBedrock #Denodo #DataVirtualization #AIAgents #FederatedQuery

Source: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Denodo and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Strategy Mosaic powers agentic AI on AWS via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Strategy Mosaic powers agentic AI on AWS via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

The latest walkthrough shows how Strategy Mosaic can serve as a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS, letting a Strands agent hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore query a Customer‑360 (C360) domain across Amazon Redshift and Amazon Aurora without ETL.

🔍 Overview

  • This post is co‑written with Zhili Cheng, Principal Product Manager, George Earle, Director, AI Engineering, and Kyler K, Sales Engineer of Strategy.
  • Mosaic implements a dimensional semantic model – attributes, hierarchies, facts and metrics – composed through Strategy’s metric expression syntax.
  • A single Mosaic definition publishes four native protocols:
    • Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI agents
    • JDBC/ODBC over Trino for SQL clients
    • XMLA for Power BI and Excel
    • REST for custom applications
  • The walkthrough reuses the C360 pattern introduced in earlier posts that used Stardog and Denodo, but now applies Mosaic’s linked‑model pattern.

🧩 How it works

  • Two Mosaic Models are created – one over Amazon Redshift, one over Amazon Aurora – and linked together.
  • Metric syntax supports:
    • Base metrics (e.g., Purchase Amount = price * quantity)
    • Advanced metrics with named filter objects and level qualifiers
    • Compound metrics that combine other metrics
  • The Strands agent reaches Mosaic through the MCP endpoint; joins, metric definitions, and per‑caller row and column filters reside in Mosaic, not in the prompt.
  • User identity flows from the enterprise identity provider through AgentCore Identity, enabling Row‑Level Security (RLS) and Object‑Level Security (OLS) to be enforced end‑to‑end.
  • Execution can be tuned between live pushdown (leveraging the underlying warehouse) and in‑memory execution for agent traffic.
  • The same governed definitions can be published to Power BI, Tableau, notebooks, and custom apps, and exported in Apache Ossie format for tools outside Mosaic.

⚙️ Key details

Item Details
Semantic layer type Dimensional (attributes, hierarchies, facts, metrics)
Modeling path Mosaic Models (self‑service, AI‑assisted) inherit dimensions, ACLs, RLS from Mosaic Schema
Forms ID form for joins, display form for reading; forms resolve names like “Carolyn Inworth” to the underlying cid
Supported systems Cloud warehouses: Snowflake, Databricks; Operational databases: Amazon RDS, Oracle, SQL Server; Analytical engines: Amazon Athena, Trino, SAP HANA; SaaS sources: Salesforce
Protocols MCP for agents, JDBC/ODBC over Trino for SQL, XMLA for Power BI/Excel, REST for custom apps
Source of truth Strategy One (March 2026) release – Mosaic access through the MCP server is enabled by default

🚀 Availability

  • The walkthrough runs on AWS services: Amazon Redshift Serverless for analytical C360 data, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as the operational system of record, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosting the Strands agent.
  • Deployment uses the native AWS data services; no ETL is required to keep the analytical copy current.
  • The MCP server is available by default in the Strategy One release.

This post continues the series that previously demonstrated semantic layers built with Stardog’s ontology‑based knowledge graph and Denodo’s data‑virtualization platform.

#AIagents #SemanticLayer #AWS #Bedrock #StrategyMosaic

item.title: AI Labs Buying Data from Defunct Startups as New Market Emerges
item.description:
AI Labs Buying Data from Defunct Startups as New Market Emerges

AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models, turning the end‑of‑life ecosystem into a nascent data‑resale market.

🔍 Overview

  • When crypto startup founder Keelan Miskell wound down his company, he sold the code base for about $25,000 and a pending ~$15,000 for workspace data (Google, Notion, Figma, Slack) through SimpleClosure.
  • SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April and now runs an Asset Hub platform that lets founders sell code and workspace data such as emails, chats, and documents.
  • Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that build simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models.

🧩 How the Market Works

  • SimpleClosure brokered over 150 deals and expects to return > $10 million to startups by the end of 2026.
  • 47 % of SimpleClosure’s deals now include code or data sales, according to CEO Dori Yona.
  • Rival Sunset also runs a data‑resale business; its CEO Brendan Mahony values assets by head count, years in operation, data volume, and tool usage, likening the exhaust data to “particle board.”
  • Demand surged last year as AI labs hit limits of public and synthetic datasets.
  • Companies like Surge AI buy archives to build reinforcement‑learning gyms where agents practice tasks (e.g., debugging IT architecture, drafting appellate briefs). Lead Nick Heiner says a rich Slack history can be more valuable than a combination of Slack, email, and calendars.

📊 Key Statistics

Metric Figure
Annual rise in startup shutdowns 26 %–56 % (Carta & AngelList)
Deals that include code/data (SimpleClosure) 47 %
Asset Hub deals handled >150
Expected return to startups (2026) > $10 M

🤝 Notable Deals & Players

  • Google outbid Mercor for Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy data: 100 M emails, 500 M Teams messages, 176 k employee records for $10 M (August).
  • SpaceX AI unit is reportedly weighing data purchases from struggling startups (September, Bloomberg).
  • Surge AI purchases real‑world archives to avoid synthetic‑world errors; pricing varies because valuations are based on research theses about task usefulness.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Attorneys like Greg Ewing call the data “legally radioactive,” noting that even after scrubbing, private details (doctor appointments, school pickups, date‑night plans) can remain.
  • Proceeds typically flow to senior creditors and investors, not to employees.
  • Law professor Ifeoma Ajunwa describes the practice as “captured capital” and argues that employers should obtain explicit consent before selling workers’ data, though no federal law currently bans such sales.
  • Founders have little visibility into who purchases their data or how it will be used.

The emerging ecosystem—coaches, “death doulas,” legal and tax specialists—reflects a growing market for the operational exhaust of companies that are winding down.

#AIData #StartupClosure #MachineLearning #DataPrivacy

Source: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models

item.title: Atomic Agent Adds Snowflake Integration via Composio and MCP
item.description:
Atomic Agent Adds Snowflake Integration via Composio and MCP

Atomic Agent, the open‑source on‑device AI assistant, now supports direct interaction with Snowflake through the Composio integration and the Snowflake Model Context Protocol (MCP).

🔍 Overview

  • Atomic Agent runs on your machine and supports local models via llama.cpp.
  • Through Composio it can connect to 1,500+ apps, including Snowflake.
  • Users can issue natural‑language requests such as “list today’s new users” or “cancel a long‑running data import”; authentication is handled automatically.

🧩 How it works

  • Atomic Agent connects to Composio’s Tool Router over Streamable HTTP MCP.
  • For each request the agent discovers the appropriate tools; Composio supplies the necessary account authentication.
  • Execution and account‑connection tools obey the agent’s configured approval policy – you must review any approval prompt before the action proceeds.

⚙️ Setup & Usage

  • Requirements: Atomic Agent v0.5.6 or later, a Composio API key, and a Snowflake account.
  • Add the line below to ~/.atomic‑agent/.env, replacing the placeholder with your key, then start Atomic Agent: 
    1

    COMPOSIO_API_KEY=YOUR_COMPOSIO_API_KEY
  • In Atomic Agent, open the Integrations tab, select Composio, press e, paste the API key, and press Enter. The tools become available immediately, without a restart.
  • Ask Atomic Agent to perform an action in Snowflake. The agent searches Composio for the correct tool. On first use, a sign‑in link is returned in the chat – follow it to connect your Snowflake account, then return to Atomic Agent to continue.

🚀 Availability

  • The Hobby plan includes 100,000 tool calls per month.
  • Integration can be disabled by setting "composio": { "enabled": false } in the config; the saved key remains on disk.

📋 Tool Reference

Tool What it does
Cancel Statement Execution Cancels the execution of a running SQL statement

The Snowflake MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol, giving the agent structured and secure access to the data warehouse and service status. It enables the agent to execute SQL, explore databases and tables, track or cancel statements, inspect catalog integrations, and monitor incidents and maintenance on your behalf.

item.title: Veeam Releases Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 with Hyper-V and Azure Support
item.description:
Veeam Releases Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 with Hyper-V and Azure Support

Veeam has launched Veeam Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 as part of the Veeam Data Platform Premium Edition. This release introduces quality-of-life improvements designed to make data orchestration simpler and more flexible, featuring new stand-alone host support, direct-to-cloud restoration, and read-only repository access.

🖥️ Stand-Alone Hyper-V and Cross-Platform Recovery

Orchestrator v13.1 introduces support for a stand-alone Hyper-V host as a recovery target, accommodating both local and shared storage. This update also introduces new migration and recovery pathways:

  • Cross-Platform Restores: vSphere environments can perform cross-platform restores from vSphere VM backups to a stand-alone Hyper-V host. This enables organizations to utilize a lower-cost Hyper-V disaster recovery site to pilot potential platform migrations on a single host.
  • Direct Azure Restores: Hyper-V VM backups can now be restored directly to Azure, joining existing support for vSphere VM and Veeam Agent backups. This feature also supports script injection to the restored virtual machines.

🛡️ Read-Only Repositories and Cleanroom Protection

Building on Veeam Backup & Replication v13.1 features, object storage repositories can now connect to Orchestrator’s embedded Veeam backup server in read-only mode. This configuration provides several key advantages:

  • Continuous Access: Users maintain constant access to the latest restore points, including imported backups, to test recovery plans.
  • Cleanroom Security: Read-only access allows cleanroom recovery environments to pull current data without creating a pathway back to production.
  • Automatic Handoffs: If the production Veeam Backup & Replication server goes down, the embedded backup server can take over failover. This update keeps the data behind that handoff current automatically, eliminating the need for manual connection refreshes.

📍 Upgraded Recovery Locations

Recovery locations have received two key upgrades designed to improve precision without sacrificing automation:

  • Specific Targeting: While automatic selection remains available, users can now target recovery directly to a specific Veeam backup server and the specific repositories it manages.
  • Map From Any Source Network: This catch-all network mapping configuration option allows recovery locations to recover VMs from source networks that have not been explicitly mapped, preventing recovery processes from failing when an unexpected network is encountered.

⚙️ Simplified Day 2 Operations

Day 2 operations and maintenance tasks have been streamlined through a unified installer, a new Scheduled Tasks page, and the new Veeam Updater plug-in, which can be launched directly from the About page in the Orchestrator web UI.

Feature Capability
Update Scheduling & Automation Allows users to define maintenance windows and control when updates are installed.
Mandatory Updates Enforces required patch levels across all managed Veeam Backup & Replication components.
Bulk Update Management Allows users to update multiple infrastructure components simultaneously to streamline maintenance.

#Veeam #DisasterRecovery #HyperV #CloudBackup #DataProtection

Source: What’s New in Veeam Recovery Orchestrator v13.1

item.title: NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit Adds Amazon S3 Vectors for Persistent Agent Memory

NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit Adds Amazon S3 Vectors for Persistent Agent Memory

NVIDIA’s open‑source NeMo Agent Toolkit (NAT) now integrates Amazon S3 Vectors as a persistent memory backend, allowing agents deployed on Amazon EKS to store and retrieve long‑term knowledge with elastic scale.

item.title: Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric
item.description:
Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers infrastructure for large-scale machine learning workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). By integrating with Cloud Native Qumulo (CNQ) and Qumulo’s Cloud Data Fabric (CDF), developers can now run training compute in one AWS Region while accessing datasets stored in another without the need to copy data or modify existing code.

🧩 How it works

Cloud Data Fabric maintains a single authoritative copy of a dataset on a hub cluster and projects it to spoke clusters as a unified POSIX namespace. Through predictive caching via NeuralCache, the system learns data loader access patterns and serves data from local NVMe storage. After an initial warmup period, this architecture allows spoke clusters to achieve throughput performance equivalent to locally co-located clusters, even across high-latency network links.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resiliency: The infrastructure continuously monitors node health and automatically replaces faulty nodes to prevent hardware failures from impacting the entire cluster.
  • Performance: Training jobs using this setup reach 98–100 percent GPU utilization after a brief warmup of 100–150 batches.
  • Integration: The solution supports remote job submission via the sagemaker_ray:// protocol and provides pre-built Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards through the HyperPod Observability EKS add-on.
  • Training Frameworks: The platform supports frameworks such as SkyRL, enabling advanced techniques like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for tasks like vision-language model navigation.

item.title: End-to-End Framework Automates Business Semantic Layer Construction from Raw Logs

Researchers have introduced an end-to-end framework that fully automates the construction of a business semantic layer from raw application logs, eliminating the need for labeled training data or manual rule engineering.

Stage Process

item.title: New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors
item.description:
New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors

A new additive profile has been developed to provide evaluation semantics for Croissant, the de facto machine-readable descriptor for ML datasets.

🔍 Overview

While Croissant version 1.1 carries data use conditions—recommending ODRL and DUO—it does not specify how these are evaluated. It lacks a decision procedure, bounds on evaluation cost, outcomes for conditions an implementation cannot evaluate, records of what was checked, and information on composition with caller-side authority.

🧩 How it works

An additive profile allows a dataset to declare admitted operations and the conditions for those admissions. Key technical features include:

  • Closed Operator Set: Uses a closed set of five operators with a full decision procedure.
  • Automated Gating: A gate can decide based on the descriptor alone and record the checks performed.
  • State Space Separation: Caller-bound and data-bound policies range over non-overlapping state spaces, meaning neither permit set contains the other.

⚙️ Key details

Testing was conducted using two corpora with evidence kept apart, as well as a corpus generated from the profile’s grammar to cover every conformance clause, refusal class, and operator.

Deployment Results (nf-core pipeline)

Metric Result
Decision Accuracy Profile document decisions match the gate’s native descriptor record for record
Compatibility Stripping the layer leaves a valid Croissant document
Performance Cost 11.7 $\mu$s added cost against a 119 $\mu$s decision

Additionally, across valid cases, 552 complete decision records showed agreement between the native descriptor, profile terms, and the ODRL policy in usageInfo.

#Croissant #MLdatasets #DataGovernance #ODRL

Source: A Policy Profile for Croissant: Refusal as a Property of the Dataset

item.title: Memanto Introduces Memory Agent for Cross-Platform Agent Memory Management
item.description:
Memanto Introduces Memory Agent for Cross-Platform Agent Memory Management

Memanto has launched a Memory Agent designed to manage the memories of other agents, handling curation, conflict resolution, and expiration across different platforms.

🔍 Overview

While platforms such as Claude, Bedrock, Cursor, and various vector stores provide storage persistence, they do not manage the content of that memory. Memanto acts as a “chief of staff” for an agent fleet, ensuring agents do not hold contradictory beliefs or redo completed work.

🧩 How it works

Memanto is a second agent that runs alongside an existing fleet based on its own judgment rather than acting as a library. It operates via a daily loop enabled by memanto schedule enable to perform the following tasks:

  • Curating new memories
  • Merging duplicates across agents
  • Flagging contradictions for review
  • Resolving contradictions
  • Discarding stale data
  • Briefing agents before they act

⚙️ Key details

  • Integration: Requires no code changes, wrappers, or rewrites of the agent loop.
  • OS Support: Compatible with macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Management: memanto ui provides a local dashboard to browse, search, and audit the estate.
  • Data Portability: The estate is stored as a file. Users can use memanto memory export --okf to export data in Open Knowledge Format (plain Markdown).

🚀 Availability

Memanto includes a memanto migrate command for importing and exporting data between the following services:

Service
Mem0
Letta
Supermemory
Any OKF bundle

💡 Why it matters

Memanto addresses the gap between storage and management. It prevents scenarios where a preference from March outranks a decision from last week or where two agents believe opposite things about a service.

item.title: Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick
item.description:
Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick

Quick has introduced architectural patterns to automate the assignment of custom permissions, allowing organizations to enforce fine-grained access control across the user lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

Custom permissions enable administrators to toggle specific features on or off for individual users. This allows for precise control, such as enabling financial analysts to author reports without exporting raw data, or allowing external partners to view dashboards without accessing sharing controls.

Permissions follow a three-level hierarchy where settings are applied as follows:

  • User-level: Overrides role-level settings.
  • Role-level: Overrides account-level settings.
  • Account-level: The base level of the hierarchy.

🧩 How it works

Organizations can use four architectural patterns to automate permissions based on their specific needs:

Method Application Scenario
RegisterUser API Applies permissions during user creation via the --custom-permissions-name parameter; common for SaaS companies restricting features like GenBI and paginated reports based on pricing tiers.
UpdateAccountCustomPermission API Sets a fallback profile for any user without an explicit assignment, including those created via Just-In-Time provisioning.
UpdateRoleCustomPermission API Sets a default custom permission profile per Quick role (READER, AUTHOR, ADMIN, and PRO roles).
Event-Driven Automation Uses Amazon EventBridge and AWS Lambda to detect new group memberships (native Quick groups or AWS IAM Identity Center groups) and apply permissions dynamically.

⚙️ Key details

  • Conditional Logic: For requirements beyond native defaults—such as applying different profiles based on group membership—event-driven automation is used. This is necessary because there is no native API for assigning custom permissions directly to a Group.
  • Complementary Strategies: Role and account-level defaults (Scenario 2) and group-based automation (Scenario 3) are complementary rather than alternatives.
  • Provisioning Gaps: Because Just-In-Time federation creates a window between account creation and group assignment, Scenario 3 only triggers upon the group membership event.
  • Enterprise Scale: Account-level defaults allow large enterprises to instantly block new features, such as GenBI or connectors, for all users during security reviews without per-user automation.

#Quick #AWS #AccessControl #Automation #IAM

Source: Automate user-level custom permissions for Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store introduces UpdateRecord API for feature-level writes
item.description:
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store introduces UpdateRecord API for feature-level writes

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store has introduced the UpdateRecord API, allowing users to update specific feature values without reading or rewriting entire records.

🔍 Overview

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a fully managed repository used to store, share, and manage machine learning (ML) features, which are the processed data used for generating predictions and training models. Features are organized into Feature Groups, which are logical collections of related features used by one or more ML models.

💡 Why it matters

Until now, updating a single feature value within a feature group required a full read-modify-write cycle using PutRecord. The UpdateRecord API removes this cycle, as the client application only needs to call the API with the changed features. Features not included in the request are preserved as-is.

🧩 How it works

The Feature Store service performs the following steps during an UpdateRecord call:

  • Validates AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions.
  • Checks EventTime ordering to reject stale writes.
  • Performs an atomic merge of the provided features.

To ensure training datasets remain accurate, a full record snapshot is automatically replicated to the offline store.

⚙️ Key details

The UpdateRecord API requires the following parameters:

Parameter Description
FeatureGroupName The target feature group
RecordIdentifierValueAsString The primary key of the record to update
Features A list of one or more feature values to set (up to 100 per call)
EventTime Must be newer than the existing stored EventTime or the call is rejected with an HTTP 409 error
TtlDuration (optional) Override or set a per-record time-to-live (TTL)

Note: UpdateRecord is not an upsert; the record must already exist.

🚀 Availability

This capability is available for both online store tiers:

  • In-Memory Tier (Amazon ElastiCache-backed): Feature-level writes work on all existing In-Memory feature groups out of the box.
  • Standard Tier (Amazon DynamoDB-backed): Requires a new storage format named Standard_V2 to support feature-level writes.

Users of the Standard Tier can transition to Standard_V2 by:

  1. Using the Feature Processor SDK to read records from an existing Standard feature group and re-ingesting them into a new Standard_V2 feature group.
  2. Calling UpdateFeatureGroup with OnlineStoreConfig.StorageType = “Standard_V2” to flip the format in place. Once declared as Standard_V2, calls to PutRecord or BatchWriteRecord will update the underlying format to Standard_V2.

#AmazonSageMaker #MachineLearning #MLOps #AWS

Source: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store introduces UpdateRecord for feature-level writes | Amazon Web Services
